newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda denies attacking Sudanese border towns.
newsitem.headline: Uganda denies attacking Sudanese border towns.

text.p: Uganda denied on Monday accusations by Khartoum that it had attacked two southern Sudanese border towns in support of rebels fighting Sudan's government.
Uganda's Minister of State for Political Affairs at the presidency, Medi Kagwa, said: "We totally reject that accusation. They have tried to look for a way of justifying."
"They (Sudan) are violating our airspace and bombing us, so they are using that as camouflage. That's the usual talk they make, accusing us for their own problems."
Kampala accused Sudanese government planes of bombing northern Uganda in February but Khartoum denied doing so.
Sudan state television interrupted a broadcast late on Sunday to read an armed forces statement saying rebels had launched attacks from Uganda and Zairean areas under Ugandan influence.
"The bombing of Bazi was conducted from the Zairean towns of Ariwara and Ambakolo which are overrun by Tutsi (Zairean) rebels supported by Uganda," said the statement.
"The Ugandan forces at 5 a.m. (0300 GMT) on Sunday launched a heinous aggression on the Sudanese border town on Kaya from the Ugandan areas of Koboko and Keriwa," the statement said.

It also said the rebels, who launched a widescale offensive on the east and south in January, had attacked Kaya town on the Uganda border and were advancing on Yei, a key centre close to the Zaire border.
Kagwa said Khartoum's accusations were based on knowing that southern Sudanese rebels were very active during the dry season but he said Uganda had no intention of getting involved in the civil war.
On Sunday, the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) said they had captured Kaya and were advancing on the main southern town of Juba.

"The SPLA forces launched a simultaneous attack on Kaya and the Yei-Juba road and captured Kaya town. Our forces are three km (two miles) from Yei town. We will capture it at any time," SPLA spokesman Yassir Arman told Reuters in Eritrea.
Arman said the rebel forces also attacked Morobo and had captured Gumuni garrison on the Yei-Juba road. The headquarters of the National Tobacco Company near Gumuni was also in SPLA hands, he said.
The John Garang-led SPLA has been fighting Khartoum since 1983, demanding independence for the mainly Christian and animist south of Sudan from the Moslem and Arabised north.

Uganda's government-owned New Vision newspaper said on Monday the Ugandan army had sealed off the border with Sudan in the West Nile area and that the SPLA had attacked Sudanese positions 30 km (19 miles) from the Ugandan border.
The newspaper said residents of the northern Ugandan town of Arua were kept awake by sounds of the battles inside Sudan.
Kaya, west of the Nile, is only 30 km (19 miles) north of the Uganda border, and 70 km (43 miles) east of Yei.

Sudan has accused neighbours Eritrea, Ethiopia and Uganda of fighting alongside the rebels, who want to put pressure on the Khartoum government and spark a popular uprising to topple President Omar Hassan al-Bashir.

The three states deny involvement. Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni threatened last month to resolve his problems with Sudan on the battlefield. Khartoum and Kampala accuse each other of sheltering rebels.
